# @zakkster/lite-ring-buffer

> Pre-allocated, zero-GC circular buffer over a Float32Array. Power-of-two capacity, mask-based wrap, oldest-first bulk copy.

## Summary

`@zakkster/lite-ring-buffer` is a zero-dependency ESM micro-library that maintains a sliding window of float32 samples without allocating during steady-state operation. It is designed for telemetry windows (frame times, audio amplitudes, network RTT, mouse velocity) where the naive `Array.push + Array.shift` pattern produces O(n) shifts and per-frame GC pressure.

The buffer is backed by a single `Float32Array` whose length is the next power of two >= the requested capacity. Wrap-around uses a bitmask AND (`head & mask`) instead of a modulo. The hot-path `push(value)` performs one indexed store, a masked increment and a compare, with no allocation.

## Core API

```js
import { RingBuffer } from '@zakkster/lite-ring-buffer';

const rb = new RingBuffer(1024);            // capacity rounded up to next pow2
rb.push(42);                                // O(1), zero alloc
rb.peekNewest();                            // -> 42
rb.peekOldest();                            // -> 42 (only one sample)
rb.count;                                   // -> 1
rb.capacity;                                // -> 1024
rb.isFull();                                // -> false

const out = new Float32Array(rb.count);
rb.copyTo(out, 0);                          // oldest-first; out[0] = oldest
```

## Concepts

- **Capacity** is rounded up to the next power of two so wrap-around can use a bitmask. The original request is preserved on `.requestedCapacity`.
- **`get(offset)`** uses 0 for newest, `count-1` for oldest. Returns `undefined` if out of range. Its `number | undefined` result boxes a non-integer sample (16 B per call); in a hot loop use **`getOrDefault(offset, 0)`**, which allocates nothing.
- **`copyTo(dst, dstOffset)`** writes oldest-first. Up to 32 samples use an allocation-free scalar loop; larger copies use at most two `TypedArray.set` calls (one per ring half), each backed by a memcpy in V8. A `dst` that is not a TypedArray (an Array, a DataView, a plain object) throws `TypeError`; a too-small one throws `RangeError`. Nothing is written in either case.
- **`tryPush(value, options)`** mirrors `push` but returns `false` when the buffer is full and `options.overwrite === false`. The options argument is read by property access -- no destructuring default -- so `tryPush(v)` does not allocate.
- **`reset()`** clears the buffer and fills the backing storage with zeros so consumers that read `data` directly never see old samples.
- **`forEach(fn)` / `[Symbol.iterator]`** visit samples oldest-first, matching `copyTo`.
- **`ceilPow2(n)`** and **`MAX_CAPACITY`** (2^31) are exported helpers. Capacities above 2^31 throw `RangeError`.
- **`destroy()`** swaps the backing typed array for a shared empty `Float32Array` (not `null`) so the GC can reclaim it in long-lived applications. Calls after `destroy()` are undefined behavior; `push`, `tryPush` and `reset` no longer throw, they do nothing.

## Constraints

- ESM only.
- Stores `number` values that round-trip through float32. Integers up to 2^24 are exact; larger integers lose precision.
- NaN and +/-Infinity are stored and read back unchanged. Downstream consumers must filter NaN where it matters (e.g. min/max).
- After `destroy()` the instance is unusable.
- Not thread-safe. For cross-Worker streaming, the consumer must implement the head/mask discipline against a `SharedArrayBuffer`.

## Performance

- `push`, `tryPush(v)`, `getOrDefault(i, 0)` and `peek*` are O(1) and allocate 0 B per call in a hot loop where V8 inlines them (`npm run alloc`, Node 26.8.2; the inlining precondition is checked by `npm run inline-diff`, REPORTED, run by hand, not in `verify`). `get(i)` allocates 16 B per call on non-integer samples.
- `copyTo` is O(n). Up to 32 samples it allocates nothing; above that it is a memcpy plus one 104 B `subarray` view per ring half (104 B contiguous, 208 B wrapped).
- `npm run torture` (`test/torture.mjs`, dev-only): lite-leak retention (all 4096 churned instances tracked mid-run, exact count gated, then drained to tracker size 0; the backing `data` of 256 live instances is reclaimed after `destroy()`) and a lite-gc-profiler budget of major 0 / minor 0 over 2,000,000 ops on each of 6 gated lanes, with a control lane that must collect. `copyTo` of more than 32 samples and `get(i)` are reported, not gated. GC-count resolution is nominal: torture prints it as `res=` (the CONTROL lane's B/op divided by its minor-GC count) on the GATE line, and it depends on the V8 new-space size, so a gated lane reading minor 0 proves it allocates less than `res` B/op, not 0 B/op. `npm run alloc` is the per-op byte gate.
- 1M `push` calls into a 4096-slot buffer produce sub-MB heap growth (`npm test` = `node test/count.mjs`, count-gated: exactly 90 tests pass across `test/RingBuffer.test.js` (59) and `test/InliningTool.test.js` (31), 0 fail, 0 skipped or todo, so an empty, skipped, crashed or early-exiting file fails; it runs under `--expose-gc`; the smoke test fails, not skips, when gc is not exposed; dev scripts need Node >= 24).

## Companion libraries

- `@zakkster/lite-stats-math` -- single-pass avg/min/max/quantile over a `RingBuffer`.
- `@zakkster/lite-canvas-graph` -- zero-GC `<canvas>` waveform renderer that consumes a `RingBuffer` directly.
